title: Explain rejected image uploads before submission
outcome: When a user selects an image larger than 5 MB, the settings screen explains the limit immediately and does not send the doomed upload request. Valid images continue through the existing flow unchanged.
why: Users currently wait for a request the API will reject, and support received six reports this month.

current: Images above 5 MB enter the normal upload state.
The API returns HTTP 413 after the browser sends the file.
The UI displays a generic error.
expected: Oversized images are rejected before submission with a specific limit message.
A valid selection after an invalid one clears the error and uploads normally.

contracts: The server-side 5 MB limit remains authoritative.

in: Client-side size validation on the profile settings avatar control.
Regression coverage for an oversized file.

constraints: Keep the file input keyboard accessible.
Announce the message through the existing live region.

acceptance.criterion: Selecting a file above 5 MB shows the specific limit without making a request.
Selecting a valid file afterward clears the error and follows the normal upload path.
Keyboard and live-region behavior remain correct.

manual: Select a 6 MB JPEG and confirm the limit appears without a network request.
Select a 1 MB JPEG and confirm the error clears and upload succeeds.
Repeat with the keyboard and confirm the live region announces the error.

unknowns.question: Do the client and API already share a browser-safe size constant?
unknowns.assumption: The existing live region is the correct error surface.
unknowns.stopWhen: Satisfying the task requires changing the endpoint contract or importing server-only code into the client bundle.

required: Report the chosen source for the 5 MB value.
List every check actually run and its result.
Call out any remaining client/server mismatch risk.
